greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. We gather today in the holy company of all the saints to find our rest in the Lord.
penitential:
Lord, you are the light of your saints: Lord, have mercy.
Christ, you are the hope of those who mourn: Christ, have mercy.
Lord, you are the promise of our resurrection: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.
homily:
We begin today not with a grand theology, but with the simple, quiet image of a threshold. Think of a doorframe in your own home—the place where you might pause before stepping out into the world, or where you stand for a moment before turning in for the night. There is something profoundly human about a threshold. It is the boundary between what we know and what we are moving toward. It is the place where we adjust our coat, check our pockets, and steady our hearts before we face the wind. Today, the Church invites us to stand at the threshold of Heaven itself, looking into the lives of those who have already crossed over, those who now stand before the throne of the Lamb.

I want you to hold onto this image: the threshold. It is the place where the light of God’s glory meets the reality of our earthly waiting.

Let us be honest about the ache that brings us to this threshold today. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who carry the light of Benjamin Vo in your hearts: it has been four months since he walked through that final door into the presence of God. We know that the silence in your home is not a peaceful silence; it is a heavy, ringing absence. You wake up, and for a split second, the world feels normal, and then the reality rushes back in. You look at the places where he used to be—the desk where he coded his games, the quiet corners that still hold the echo of his brilliant, searching mind—and the weight of missing him can feel like a mountain. It is an ache that does not ask for platitudes. It is an ache that asks for the truth. And the truth is that you are grieving a loss that is as deep as the love you had for him. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to be sad. You are allowed to be human.

There is a temptation, when we carry such a weight, to look back at the path we walked and wonder if we missed a sign. We wonder if we could have seen something earlier, or done something differently, or if we failed in some hidden way. Let us lift that stone from your hearts right now. You missed nothing. You were the parents and the brother that Benjamin was given. You loved him with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of the world. You walked the globe with him, you shared the meals, you witnessed the brilliance of his mind and the gentleness of his spirit. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. The sorrow that has entered your life is not a consequence of anything you did or failed to do. You were faithful. You were present. You were love in action. Let that burden fall away, and let yourself breathe.

Now, let the Gospel break in. Jesus goes up the mountain, sits down, and begins to teach. He does not speak to the powerful or the elite. He speaks to those who are poor in spirit, those who mourn, those who hunger for righteousness. He tells them: 'Blessed are they who mourn, for they will be comforted.' This is not a distant promise for a far-off day; it is a promise for this very moment. When you mourn, you are standing in the presence of the Comforter. When you feel the weight of your loss, you are being held by the very One who wept at the grave of his friend Lazarus. Jesus knows what it is to lose someone he loved. He knows the ache of a heart that is broken by the departure of a brother. He is not standing back, waiting for you to be 'better' or to 'move on.' He is in the room with you. He is the one who lifts you up.

Benjamin was a boy who understood the beauty of connection. Think of his brilliant mind—the way he looked at the world through the lens of mathematics and logic, yet always with a heart that was soft and kind. He was a boy who, at fifteen, offered his entire piggy bank to help an uncle who was struggling. He didn't need to break the bank, he didn't need to empty it—the offer itself was the revelation of his character. It was the movement of a soul that was already living in the Kingdom of God. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who is now at the banquet of heaven, looking down at you. And just as he was a source of light and joy for you, he continues to be a source of grace. Think of the well in Cà Mau, the clean water flowing for the poor in his name. His love did not end when his life on earth did. It is still flowing. It is still quenching the thirst of the world. It is still doing the work of the Kingdom—the work of mercy, the work of healing.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess.

In our first reading today, John sees a great multitude, which no one could count, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands. They are the ones who have survived the time of great distress; they have washed their robes and made them white in the Blood of the Lamb. This is where Benjamin is. He is part of that great, uncountable multitude. He is standing in the light, he is resting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is not a memory; he is a living soul, fully alive in the love of God.

We hear in the second reading: 'Beloved, we are God's children now; what we shall be has not yet been revealed. We do know that when it is revealed we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.' This is the hope that sustains us. We are not just waiting for the end of our lives; we are waiting for the revelation of the life we have already been given in Christ. Every act of kindness you do, every prayer you whisper, every tear you shed in love—these are the ways you are making your own robes white. You are participating in the life of the saints. You are living in the communion of love that death cannot touch.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, he is waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin smiling at you from the other side. Let yourself be gathered. Trust that you are held. And walk out into the world with the quiet, unshakeable hope that the love you share is the most powerful force in the universe. It is stronger than death. It is more enduring than time. And it is the very thing that will bring you home to each other. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light of Christ’s face.
For all who are grieving, that God may console them with his presence and fill them with the hope of eternal life.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may his face shine upon you, and may you find your rest in his eternal peace. Go in the love of Christ.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, saw another angel come up from the East,

holding the seal of the living God.

He cried out in a loud voice to the four angels

who were given power to damage the land and the sea,

"Do not damage the land or the sea or the trees

until we put the seal on the foreheads of the servants of our God."

I heard the number of those who had been marked with the seal,

one hundred and forty-four thousand marked

from every tribe of the children of Israel.



After this I had a vision of a great multitude,

which no one could count,

from every nation, race, people, and tongue.

They stood before the throne and before the Lamb,

wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.

They cried out in a loud voice:



"Salvation comes from our God, who is seated on the throne,

and from the Lamb."



All the angels stood around the throne

and around the elders and the four living creatures.

They prostrated themselves before the throne,

worshiped God, and exclaimed:



"Amen. Blessing and glory, wisdom and thanksgiving,

honor, power, and might

be to our God forever and ever. Amen."



Then one of the elders spoke up and said to me,

"Who are these wearing white robes, and where did they come from?"

I said to him, "My lord, you are the one who knows."

He said to me,

"These are the ones who have survived the time of great distress;

they have washed their robes

and made them white in the Blood of the Lamb."

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (see 6) Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.

The LORD's are the earth and its fullness;

the world and those who dwell in it.

For he founded it upon the seas

and established it upon the rivers.

R. Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.

Who can ascend the mountain of the LORD?

or who may stand in his holy place?

One whose hands are sinless, whose heart is clean,

who desires not what is vain.

R. Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.

He shall receive a blessing from the LORD,

a reward from God his savior.

Such is the race that seeks him,

that seeks the face of the God of Jacob.

R. Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Beloved:

See what love the Father has bestowed on us

that we may be called the children of God.

Yet so we are.

The reason the world does not know us

is that it did not know him.

Beloved, we are God's children now;

what we shall be has not yet been revealed.

We do know that when it is revealed we shall be like him,

for we shall see him as he is.

Everyone who has this hope based on him makes himself pure,

as he is pure.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
When Jesus saw the crowds, he went up the mountain,

and after he had sat down, his disciples came to him.

He began to teach them, saying:



"Blessed are the poor in spirit,

for theirs is the Kingdom of heaven.

Blessed are they who mourn,

for they will be comforted.

Blessed are the meek,

for they will inherit the land.

Blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness,

for they will be satisfied.

Blessed are the merciful,

for they will be shown mercy.

Blessed are the clean of heart,

for they will see God.

Blessed are the peacemakers,

for they will be called children of God.

Blessed are they who are persecuted for the sake of righteousness,

for theirs is the Kingdom of heaven.

Blessed are you when they insult you and persecute you

and utter every kind of evil against you falsely because of me.

Rejoice and be glad,

for your reward will be great in heaven."

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.
